 JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under the provisions of Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation of Rs.70,00,000/ for the death of Babanna @ Babu caused in a Road Traffic accident.

Smt. Thimmakka vs Cholamandalam Ms on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151426364/
2 2.

The brief facts of the petitioners case are as under:
It is the case of the petitioners that on 04.01.2019 around 4.00 pm., the Petitioner No.1 and Petitioner No.3 as a pillion rider and the deceased Babanna @ Babu as a rider were returning to their village in a Bajaj Discover Motor cycle from Amarapuram after visiting the hospital.

When they reached near petrol bunk at SCCH - 26 4 MVC No.2727/2020 about 6.30 pm., a Tractor being driven by its driver at high speed and in a rash and negligent manner came from opposite direction and dashed against their motor cycle.
Due to impact, the deceased fell on the ground and sustained grievous injuries and Petitioner No.1 and 3 also sustained injuries.
Immediately the injured persons shifted to Madakasira government hospital and from their to deceased was shifted to Pinnacle hospital, Bangalore but he died while taking treatment on 10.01.2019.
They incurred sum of Rs.3,00,000/ for providing treatment to the deceased.
Thereafter, the post mortem was conducted on the body of the deceased and handed over to them.
3. Further it is stated in the petition that thereafter, they spent sum of Rs.1,00,000/ towards transportation of body of deceased and for funeral and other ceremonies.
It is further stated in the petition that prior to the accident, deceased was hale and healthy and was working as coolie and earning sum of SCCH - 26 5 MVC No.2727/2020 Rs.500/ per day.
Due to his death, petitioner No.1 lost her beloved husband and petitioner No.2 to 4 lost their beloved father and petitioner No.5 lost his beloved son and Petitioner No.6 and 8 lost their brother.

Further, it is stated in the petition that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of driver of tractor and trailer and in this regard FIR in crime No.1/2019 came to be registered at Amarapuram police station against the driver of the tractor and trailer for the offence punishable under section 337 and 304(A) of IPC.
The Respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending tractor and trailer and Respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending tractor are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, petitioners have prayed to award compensation of Rs.70 lakhs from the respondents.
4. The summons of the petition has been duly served on respondent No.1 and 2.
The Respondent No.1 has appeared before this tribunal and filed his SCCH - 26 6 MVC No.2727/2020 written statement.
He has admitted that he issued insurance policy with respect to tractor bearing reg.No.AP02CK1282 as such, his liability to subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further he has contended that, the owner of the vehicle or the police have not complied with the provisions of IMV Act after the alleged accident.
He has denied the entire averments of the petition as false and baseless.
Further he has contended that the Petitioners in collusion with the owner of the vehicle, hospital authorities and the police created documents only to get compensation.
He has also contended that the driver of the tractor was not having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
He has further contended that, the Respondent No.2 knowingly entrusted his vehicle to a person who was not possessing valid and effective driving licence as such, he committed breach of policy.
Further he has contended that if this tribunal pleases to award compensation then the rate of interest may be restricted to 6% per annum.
Hence, he has prayed to SCCH - 26 7 MVC No.2727/2020 dismiss the petition.

Smt. Thimmakka vs Cholamandalam Ms on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151426364/
3 5.
The respondent No.2 has filed his written statement admitting his ownership with respect to the tractor and trailer.
Further he has denied the rest of the petition averments as false and baseless.
He has also contended that the accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the deceased but not on the part of the driver of the tractor.
He has also contended that the Petitioners have created false documents to claim the compensation.
Hence, he has prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. Based on the above pleadings of both the parties, my predecessor in office has framed the following issues :
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioners proves that, deceased Babanna @ Babu S/o Sanna Lingappa, aged about 39 years, was dies in a road traffic accident that occurred on 0401 2019 at about 06.30 p.m. deceased was riding the vehicle, when he reached at Amarapuram to Hemavathi Road, near Petrol Bunk, Amarapuram village and Mandal, at SCCH - 26 8 MVC No.2727/2020 that time the driver of the Tractor bearing No.AP02AC1282 driven in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased's vehicle.
As a result deceased sustained fatal injuries and died, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition?

If so,
from which respondent?
3. What Order or Award?
7. The Petitioner No.1 has got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 19 documents as Ex's.P1 to 19.

On the other hand the Deputy Manager of respondent No.1 has got examined himself as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 and Record Assistant, Government Hospital has got examined himself as RW.2 and got marked 3 documents as Ex.R.2 to 4.
8.
Heard the arguments from both sides.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

9. My answers to the above issues are as follows :
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative SCCH - 26 9 MVC No.2727/2020 Issue No.2 : Partly Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.1: As already stated supra Petitioner No.1 in order to prove the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of offending trator and trailer he has examined herself as PW.1.
She has filed affidavit for her chief examination reiterating the entire averments of petition.
She has go marked 19 document as Ex.P.1 to 19 in support of her version.

Smt. Thimmakka vs Cholamandalam Ms on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151426364/
4 11.

PW.1 in her evidence has stated that, on 04.01.2019 around 4.00 pm., she and Petitioner No.3 as a pillion rider and her husband deceased Babanna @ Babu as a rider were returning to their village in a Bajaj Discover Motor cycle from Amarapuram after visiting the hospital.

Further she has deposed that, when they reached near petrol bunk at about 6.30 pm., a Tractor bearing No.AP02 CK1282 being driven by its SCCH - 26 10 MVC No.2727/2020 driver at high speed and in a rash and negligent manner came from opposite direction and dashed against their motor cycle and due to impact, the deceased fell on the ground and sustained grievous injuries and died at the hospital while taking treatment.

Further she has deposed that she and Petitioner No.3 sustained injuries and in this regard FIR came to be registered against the driver of the Tractor bearing No.AP02CK 1282 at jurisdictional police station.

In support of her evidence she has produced true copy of FIR,
compliant, translated copy of complaint, alteration memo, rough sketch, death intimation, IMV report, inquest report, translated copy of inquest report, PM report and charge sheet which are marked at Ex.P.1 to 10.
12.

From the evidence on record it can be seen that after receipt of complaint lodged by PW.1, the Amarapuram police have registered FIR in Crime No.1/2019 against the driver of Tractor bearing No.AP 02CK1282 for the offences punishable u/s 337 of IPC.

SCCH - 26 11 MVC No.2727/2020 After due investigation the police have filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending Tractor bearing No.AP02CK1282 for the offences punishable u/s 337,
304(A) of IPC.
Ex.P.4 is the rough sketch which shows that the accident took place on the middle of the Amarapuram road.
The IMV report marked at Ex.P.6 shows that the accident occurred not due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles.
Ex.P.7 is the inquest report and Ex.P.9 is the PM report of deceased Babanna.
As per these documents the deceased died due to head injury sustained in road traffic accident.
Though the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has cross examined PW1 but he has failed to elicit anything from her to disbelieve her version.
Further she has clearly denied the suggestion that due to the negligence on the part of the deceased, the accident had occurred.
13. On the other hand the Deputy Manager of Respondent No.1 has examined himself as RW.1.
He SCCH - 26 12 MVC No.2727/2020 has deposed that as on the date of accident the policy issued by the Respondent No.1 with respect to tractor bearing reg.No.AP02CK1282 was valid.
He has produced the said policy certificate at Ex.R.1.

Further he has deposed that, the tractor bearing reg.No.AP02 CK1282 was falsely implicated in this case in collusion with owner of the vehicle,
hospital authority and the police.
He has also deposed that the Petitioners have not assigned any reason for one day delay in lodging the complaint.
The learned counsel for the Petitioners has cross examined RW.1.
In his cross examination he has admitted that, he is having the knowledge of this case based on the police documents.
Further he has admitted that he did not challenge the charge sheet filed by the police in this case.
Though the Respondent No.1 has contended that the tractor bearing reg.No.AP 02CK1282 was falsely implicated in this case but he has not produced any evidence to prove the same before this tribunal.
Therefore, there is nothing on record to show that the chargesheet filed by the police SCCH - 26 13 MVC No.2727/2020 is collusive or defective.
From the evidence adduced by the Petitioners it is clear that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending tractor bearing reg.No.AP02CK1282.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while Smt. Thimmakka vs Cholamandalam Ms on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151426364/
5 deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compared to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the chapter in M.V.Act dealing with compensation is a benevolent legislation and not a penal one.
Therefore, based on the above discussion, I hold that the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the tractor bearing reg.No.AP02CK1282 is proved.
As such, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
14. ISSUE NO.2:
PW.1 has produced notarised copies of Aadhar cards at Ex.P.11 to 19.

As per these documents it is clear that Petitioner is the wife of deceased Babanna, Petitioner No.2 to 4 are their minor SCCH - 26 14 MVC No.2727/2020 children, Petitioner No.5 is the father of deceased Babanna and Petitioner No.6 to 8 are brothers of the deceased.
It is relevant to note that Petitioner No6 to 8 major brothers of deceased.
Hence, they cannot be considered as dependents on the deceased.
Therefore, Petitioner No.1 to 5 are alone considered as dependants on the income of deceased.
As such, Petitioner No.1 to 5 are entitled for compensation under the head loss of dependency.
15. LOSS OF DEPENDENCY:
Ex.P.19 is the notarized copy of Aadhar card of deceased.
This document does not disclose the exact date of birth of the deceased.
However, this document shows the birth of year of deceased as 1984.
As per PM report marked at Ex.P.9 the age of the deceased is shown as 35 years.
Hence, it indicates that the deceased was aged about 35 years.

Therefore, the appropriate multiplier as per Sarala Verma's case for the said age group is "16".
16.
According to PW.1 her deceased husband SCCH - 26 15 MVC No.2727/2020 was doing coolie and earning Rs.500/ per day.
To prove the same PW.1 has not produced any document.
Even she has not adduced any witnesses to show the income and avocation of the deceased.
In the absence of proof of avocation and income, this tribunal has to consider notional income for calculating the compensation.
As per the guidelines issued by Karnataka State Legal Service Authority the notional income of the deceased is taken as Rs.14,000/ as the accident took place in the year 2019.
17. In the present case the deceased was aged about 35 years.
His notional income is taken as Rs.14,000/ p.m.

As per the Hon'ble Apex court reported in a decision reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court cases 680 (National Insurance company Ltd., Vs Pranay Sethi and others), 25% of income is to be added towards future prospects as the deceased was self employed.

sentences.text:
Therefore, 25%
of Rs.14,000/ works out to Rs.3,500/.
Therefore the total income of the SCCH - 26 16 MVC No.2727/2020 deceased works out to Rs.17,500/ (Rs.14,000/ + Rs.3,500/).
Since the petitioner No.1 to 5 are the dependents of the deceased, the 1/4th of the total salary is to be deducted towards his personal expenses.
Hence, 1/4th of Rs.17,500/ works out to Rs.4,375/.
Income for consideration is Rs.13,125/ (17,500/ ()  4,375/).

Annual income works out to Rs.1,57,500/
(13,125/ x 12).
Appropriate multiplier is "16".
Thus loss of dependency worksout to Rs.25,20,000/ (1,57,500 x 16).
18. LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:

It is relevant to note that due to the death of deceased, petitioner No.1 lost her beloved husband and petitioner No.2 to 4 lost their beloved father and they have also lost their parental aid, protection, affection, discipline, guidance and training.
Similarly, petitioner No.5 has lost his beloved son and Petitioner No.6 to 8 lost their beloved brother.

Therefore, in view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex court in civil Appeal SCCH - 26 17 MVC No.2727/2020 Smt. Thimmakka vs Cholamandalam Ms on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151426364/
6 No.2705/2020 in the case of United India Insurance company Ltd., Vs Satinder Kaur and others,
each of the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/ on account of loss of consortium and loss of love and affection.

sentences.text: 19. LOSS OF ESTATE: Petitioners are entitled for Rs.15,000/ towards loss of estate.
20. FUNERAL EXPENSES:
Petitioners are entitled for Rs.15,000/ towards funeral expenses.

21. The calculation table stands as follows : 1 Loss of dependency Rs. 25,20,000 =00 2 Loss of consortium Rs. 3,20,000=00 Rs.40,000/ each) 3 Loss of estate Rs. 15,000=00 4 Funeral expenses Rs. 15,000=00 GRAND
TOTAL Rs. 28,70,000=00 Hence, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.28,70,000 /.

22. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY: Having SCCH - 26 18 MVC No.2727/2020 regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.

23. The respondent No.2 is the RC owner of offending tractor and respondent No.1 is insurer of the said tractor and it is admitted fact that as on the date of the accident, the offending tractor was having valid insurance policy.

Therefore respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 'in the Partly affirmative'.
24. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
 SCCH - 26 19 MVC No.2727/202  : ORDER :
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.28,70,000/ (Rupees Twenty Eight Lakhs Seventy Thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
